grh_7c71f13250392ee0e696.title: Melody Ranch - Ragtime Cowboy Joe 50-09-30
paragraphs: Gene opens this Melody Ranch broadcast with 'Ragtime Cowboy Joe' and mixes music and comedy with a western story about old prospector Caleb Hooten, whom Gene once found panning for gold with his mule Clarence. When Caleb later disappears, Gene checks the county claims office and finds that the Sandy Creek ground has supposedly been filed by another man; because the filing is dated on the state's Admission Day holiday, when the government office would have been closed, Gene realizes the claim is fraudulent. He uses Johnny Bond and a newly filed mining claim as bait to trap the swindlers, clears up Caleb's disappearance and property fraud, and ends with more western music and the Melody Ranch signoff.

This [[show|melody-ranch|Melody Ranch]] broadcast aired on September 30, 1950. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Parker Fennelly, The King Sisters, Johnny Bond, The Cass County Boys, and Gene Autry. Other credited names include William Burch as director and Charles Stark as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.15ec53f734045c92|Doublemint gum]].

grh_7c3b670e80e1a9965289.title: Silver Threads
paragraphs: When Homer Danfield is shot and robbed, the one usable clue is a tune associated with the attack: 'Silver Threads Among the Gold.' Britt remembers itinerant guitarist Toby Yeager teaching him that same song and helps the sheriff track him down. Singing the tune alone is not proof, and Toby initially seems to have a plausible explanation for his movements. Then a local poker player reveals that Toby lost his entire railroad pay the night of the shooting, while Toby is now carrying forty-eight unexplained dollars. Confronted with that contradiction, Toby admits that he shot Homer.

This [[show|the-six-shooter|The Six Shooter]] broadcast aired on June 3, 1954. It is listed as episode 36 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Britt Ponset]].
